attachesAs: a vertical stroke with a small top hook, written after the consonant
compositionOrder: write the Tamil consonant carrier first
write the aa sign after it, as a symbol of its own to the right

compositionSource.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0 User Manual, sections 4 and 4-3 and Table 3: vowel signs that occur as distinct characters to the left or right of the base consonant are recognizer symbols of their own, and syllabic units are written from left to right
compositionSource.variation: Table 3 lists U+0BBE, U+0BBF, U+0BC0, U+0BC6, U+0BC7 and U+0BC8 as symbols of their own, and HP Labs India's notes on the hpl-tamil-iso-char dataset add that these signs leave Tamil 'written linearly as a sequence of visually discrete symbols'. So a sign placed left of its consonant is written before it, and a sign placed right of it is written after it. The manual gives no path for the consonant and no order for a sign fused with its consonant, such as u or the ligature ti.

strokeOrder: start partway down the left upright and draw down to its foot
without lifting, climb back up and carry the top bar to the right
without lifting, come back to the right upright and draw it down — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one continuous stroke — three joined movements, no pen lift; cited to native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer, class 36

strokeOrderSource.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 36 (ா, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 189 of the 217 stored prototypes of the aa sign (87%) are one pen-down stroke. In 135 of those 189 the pen starts on the left, partway down, and first moves down; 154 end at the foot of the right upright. So the left upright is drawn down, climbed back to the top bar, and the right upright comes last, without lifting. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline, whose top bar runs a little past the right upright. Handwriting varies by writer.
